property_summary: After getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) followed by withdrawReward(recipient), the reward balance is zeroed so the contract's ETH balance drops by exactly the bonus (100 wei) plus the initial reward amount only once; the mutant re-credits the withdrawn amount so a subsequent withdrawReward pays it out again, changing the contract's balance.

For any caller, after a recipient's reward has been withdrawn once, a subsequent withdrawReward(recipient) pays nothing (zero amount), so even a receiver that rejects any nonzero transfer accepts the second call; the mutant re-credits the withdrawn amount and pays it again, making the second call revert.

After a successful withdrawReward, a recipient's reward is permanently zero, so any subsequent withdrawReward to that recipient transfers nothing and succeeds even against a receiver that rejects nonzero payments; the mutant re-credits the withdrawn amount so the second withdrawal re-pays and is rejected by such a receiver.

Because withdrawReward zeroes the reward before paying, a re-entrant call back into withdrawReward during the payout transfers nothing extra, so the contract's balance drops by exactly the reward once; the mutant re-credits the reward so the re-entrant call pays it again, draining double.

For any recipient, once a reward has been withdrawn the reward balance is zero, so any subsequent withdrawReward(recipient) transfers nothing and leaves address(c).balance unchanged; the mutant re-credits the withdrawn amount so a repeat withdrawal pays again and drains an extra 100 wei.

For any recipient behavior, a reentrant call back into c during a payout must be rejected (the outer call reverts); the reference C enforces this via its reentrancy lock, while the mutant (which removed the lock) lets the reentrant call succeed.

For any caller, calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus on a recipient that re-enters the same function during the payout must revert (the reentrancy lock blocks the nested payout and bonus), but the mutant without the require(!_locked) check lets the reentrant call succeed and the outer call return true.

Calling withdrawReward on an address with zero pending reward must succeed (a 0-value call returns success) and must leave the reentrancy lock released; in M the inverted check makes this call revert.
Each address can claim the first-withdrawal bonus at most once: a second getFirstWithdrawalBonus call for the same recipient must revert.
